<Rep. Robert C. "Bobby" Scott, Rep. Suzanne Bonamici, Rep. Mark DeSaulnier, Rep. Jahana Hayes, Rep. John W. Mannion>: H.R. 6472 Improves College Affordability for Students from U.S.
Territories
H.R. 6472, the Territorial Student Access to Higher Education Act, amends the Higher Education Act of 1965 (HEA) to require states to offer in-state tuition rates for certain residents of Guam, the Northern Mariana Islands, American Samoa, and the U.S. Virgin Islands. Specifically, the newly created HEA section 135A would prohibit any public institution of higher education that receives funding under the HEA from charging any covered individual a tuition rate that is greater than the rate charged for residents of the State in which such institution is located.\1\ The bill defines ``covered individual'' as someone who is a resident of Guam, the Commonwealth of the Northern Mariana Islands, American Samoa, or the U.S. Virgin Islands and is a national of the United States (as defined in section 101(a) of the Immigration and Nationality Act).\2\ The legislation also amends section 487(a) of the HEA to tie this new 135A requirement to an institution's Program Participation Agreement (PPA), which determines their eligibility to receive federal student aid under HEA title IV (Title IV).\3\
\1\H.R. 6472, Sec. 1, 119th Cong. (2025).
\2\Id.
\3\Id.
Committee Democrats support efforts to improve college affordability for underrepresented students and unanimously voted in favor of H.R. 6472 at markup. However, it is important to note that although this legislation would increase college affordability and access for students across these territories, it comes after Congressional Republicans made it harder for these same students to afford higher education due to Pell Grant cuts, loan limit changes, and the elimination of affordable loan repayment plans in H.R. 1.\4\
\4\Pub. L. No. 119-21 Title VIII (2025).
The Federal Government Should Fund H.R. 6472
Despite our support for H.R. 6472's goal of improving college affordability, Committee Democrats would take a different approach to supporting in-state tuition rates for certain populations of out-state students. While Democrats support increased access to higher education, H.R. 6472 places an unfunded mandate on states to implement the policy. Each state has the right to decide where and to whom their respective funding goes to and despite declines in state investment in higher education over the decades, states provide most of the funding for public higher education. Given the outsized role of states in public higher education, the significant concerns public higher education leaders have expressed with the federal government superseding state residency requirements and in-state tuition prices should not be ignored.\5\ This is especially concerning since it is the federal government who exercises primary jurisdiction over the territories--not states. Thus, should Congress want to mandate in-state tuition for residents of certain US territories, Committee Democrats believe Congress should provide federal funding for the implementation of such a policy.\6\
\5\Letter from Dr. Waded Cruzado, Pres., Assoc. of Public and Land-grant Univs. & Dr. Charles L. Welch, Pres. & CEO, Am. Assoc. of State Coll. & Univs., to Rep. Tim Walberg, Chair., H. Comm. on Educ. & Workforce and Rep. Bobby Scott, Ranking Member, H. Comm. on Educ. & Workforce (Dec. 10, 2025), https://www.aplu.org/members/councils/ governmental-affairs/cga-library/aplu-and-aascu-letter-on-education-workforce-tuition-mandate/.
\6\The policy goal of ensuring that the federal government bears the costs associated with certain out-of-state residents receiving in-state tuition pricing is not a new one. Although it is not in the jurisdiction of the Committee, the federal government provides tuition assistance grants to eligible District of Columbia students to subsidize the cost of attending out-of-state institutions. See District of Columbia College Access Act of 1999, Pub. L. No. 106-98 (1999). Most recently, Congress appropriated $40 million for this program in Fiscal Year 2026. Press Release, Norton Secures Victories in Senate D.C. Appropriations Bill, Del. Eleanor Holmes Norton, Nov. 26, 2025, https:/ /norton.house.gov/media/press-releases/norton-secures-victories-senate-dc-appropriations-bill.
Committee Democrats previously made efforts to lower tuition rates for students from outlying areas in the 117th Congress while considering the Build Back Better Act.\7\ Committee Democrats passed out of Committee a provision to invest $40,000,000 to cover the difference between in-state and out-of-state tuition for first-time students from the Northern Mariana Islands, American Samoa, U.S. Virgin Islands, and Guam who attend an out-of-state, four-year, public college.\8\ Students would receive a maximum benefit of $15,000 per year and $75,000 total to ensure their tuition rate is equal to the in-state tuition rate. To be eligible, the student must have lived in the outlying area for at least one year prior to college enrollment, enroll in college within three years of graduating high school or transferring from a college in an outlying area, and enroll in college on at least a half-time basis. This provision, while not ultimately included in the final version of the legislation, the Inflation Reduction Act, serves as a better starting point to support lowering the cost of college for this student population.
\7\Build Back Better Act, S. Con. Res. 14, Sec. 20024, (as reported by the H. Comm. on Educ. & Lab., Sept. 9, 2021) https://docs.house.gov/ meetings/ED/ED00/20210909/114029/BILLS-117 CommitteePrintih.pdf.
\8\Id.
Democratic Amendment Offered During Markup of H.R. 6472
During the markup of H.R. 6472, Rep. Alma Adams (D-NC) put forward an amendment to require the federal government to annually reimburse public institutions of higher education for any revenue lost as a result of requiring in-state tuition rates for covered individuals. This would have ensured that the federal government, not states, fund this federally determined benefit. Committee Republicans rejected this amendment.
